newsitem.title: USA: US stocks seen opening higher.
newsitem.headline: US stocks seen opening higher.

text.p: U.S. stocks were expected to open higher on the final "Merger Monday" of 1996, fueled by activity in takeover stocks after two big mergers were announced over the weekend.

Brooklyn Union Gas Co and Long Island Lighting Co (LILCO) agreed to merge to create a $4 billion electric and gas company, and Dutch insurer Aegon NV agreed to buy the insurance activities of Providian Corp in a deal worth $3.5 billion.
The Dow Industrials' small rise on Friday was enough to set a new record closing high, with the index up 14 points to about 6561, topping its previous record close of 6547.79 set on November 25.
"I'm looking for a higher opening. The market certainly wants to inch up here although it's still pretty quiet," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments.
The March futures index of the Standard & Poor's 500 Index, often a reliable indicator of opening sentiment, was up 1.3 to 765.90.
The long bond was up 3/32 to yield 6.53 percent.

The November Index of Leading Indicators, due at 0830 EST/1330 GMT, is forecast to rise 0.1 percent. November existing home sales, due at 1000 EST/1500 GMT, are expected to rise to an annual rate of 3.97 million.
The data were expected to have little impact on bonds unless they came in significantly over or under estimates, analysts said.

"I think we're going to have a continuation of what we've been seeing over the past 10 days -- a flurry of buying that takes the averages up in the morning but gives up most of its intraday gains by the end of the day," Cardillo said.
He said chances were good for another record close today, especially due to activity in takeover and merger stocks.
Tokyo stocks closed a whisper lower in their final 1996 session, falling 7.69 points, or 0.04 percent, to 19,361.35
The dollar was firm against the yen, above 116 at midday in European trading, and steady against the mark.
Banks led Hong Kong stocks to a higher close with the Hang Seng Index jumping 76.61 points to close at 13,480.75.

London shares were stronger, with U.K. blue chips holding gains and remaining near a new record high set earlier today, supported by takeover speculation surrounding British Aerospace and strong index futures.

U.S. shares traded in London were mostly firmer, but trading volumes remained thin. Oil stocks were strong, with Exxon, Atlantic Richfield and Texaco all rising slightly as investors anticipated strong fourth quarter earnings in light of surging crude prices.

The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street column said Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway Inc may be a victim of its own success. The company posted gains of a mere 3.0 percent for 1996, perhaps because it jumped 58 percent in 1995, the newspaper said.
